2.3 The Rezk axiom

The notions of identity morphisms and composition of morphisms in categories, provided by the Segal axiom, lead to the notion of an isomorphism in a category:

Definition 2.3.1 (Isomorphisms). Consider a morphism \(f\colon x \to y\) in a category \(C\). We say that \(f\) is invertible, or that it is an isomorphism, if there are commutative triangles in \(C\) of the form

Agda Invertible morphisms

IsInvertible

Definition, checked

record IsInvertible {C : CAT} {x y : Obj-abs C} (f : Morphism x y) : Set m where
  field
    right-inverse : Morphism y x
    left-inverse : Morphism y x
    right-inverse-triangle : CompositeWitness right-inverse f (identity-morphism y)
    left-inverse-triangle : CompositeWitness f left-inverse (identity-morphism x)

An invertible natural transformation is called a natural isomorphism. The Rezk axiom will relate invertible morphisms to the primitive identifications of objects from Definition 1.1.2. We start by defining the category \(\Iso (C)\) of isomorphisms in \(C\).

    left-inverse : Morphism y x
    right-inverse-triangle : CompositeWitness right-inverse f (identity-morphism y)

Definition 2.3.2. Given a category \(C\), we define the category \(\Iso (C)\) via the following pullback diagram:

Agda The category of isomorphisms

Iso

Definition, checked

Iso : CAT → CAT
Proof / implementation
Iso C = Pullback (inverseLongEdges C) (inverseIdentityEdges C)

Notice that by definition a morphism \(f \in \Ar (C)\) is invertible in \(C\) if and only if it lifts to an absolute object of \(\Iso (C)\). We may therefore think of the fiber of \(\pi _{\Iso }\) over \(f\) as the category of ‘proofs that \(f\) is invertible’. The following lemma shows that there is at most one such proof:

Agda A lift to the isomorphism category

IsoLift

Definition, checked

record IsoLift {Γ C : CAT} (f : MAP Γ (Ar C)) : Set m where
  field
    lift : MAP Γ (Iso C)
    comparison : (isoArrow ∘ lift) =₁ f

invertible-lift

Derivation, checked

invertible-lift : {C : CAT} {x y : Obj-abs C} (f : Morphism x y) →

Proof

Proof. We use the unit and associativity comparisons over prescribed vertices established in Lemma 2.2.6 and Proposition 2.2.7. We need to show that the diagonal \[ \Delta \colon \Iso (C) \to \Iso (C) \times _{\Ar (C)} \Iso (C) \] is an equivalence, or equivalently that the first projection \[ \pr _1\colon \Iso (C) \times _{\Ar (C)} \Iso (C) \to \Iso (C) \] is an equivalence. To this end, consider the two functors \begin {align*} \Ar (C) \times _{\ev _1,C,\ev _0} \Iso (C) &\to \Ar (C) \times _{\ev _1,C,\ev _1} \Iso (C), \qquad (g,f) \mapsto (f \circ g, f) \\ \Iso (C) \times _{\ev _1,C,\ev _0} \Ar (C) &\to \Iso (C) \times _{\ev _0,C,\ev _0} \Ar (C), \qquad (f,h) \mapsto (f,h \circ f). \end {align*}

We claim that these functors are equivalences. For the first functor, note that for \(f \in \Iso (C)\) we may functorially extract both a left inverse \(f_l\) with an identification \(f_l \circ f = \id _{s(f)}\) as well as a right inverse \(f_r\) with an identification \(f \circ f_r = \id _{t(f)}\). Using associativity of composition, a left inverse to the first functor is then given by \((g' ,f) \mapsto (f_l \circ g', f)\), while a right inverse is given by \((g',f) \mapsto (f_r \circ g', f)\). One argues similarly for the second functor.

The claim now follows from the observation that the projection \(\pr _1\) is the left vertical map in the following pullback square, where the right vertical map is the fiber product over \(\Iso (C)\) of the two equivalences just constructed, hence an equivalence itself:

□

As one expects, the identity morphism of any term \(\Gamma \vdash x:C\) is invertible in the same context:

Agda Identity morphisms are invertible

Derivation, checked

identity-isInvertible : {C : CAT} (x : Obj-abs C) → IsInvertible (identity-morphism x)
Proof / implementation
identity-isInvertible x = record
  { right-inverse = identity-morphism x ; left-inverse = identity-morphism x
  ; right-inverse-triangle = morphism-left-unit (identity-morphism x)
  ; left-inverse-triangle = morphism-left-unit (identity-morphism x) }

Corollary 2.3.6. For functors \(f,g\colon C\to D\), there is an equivalence \[ (f=g)\simeq *\times _{\Fun (C,D)\times \Fun (C,D)}\Iso (\Fun (C,D)), \] where the maps defining the fiber product are \((f,g)\) and \((\ev _0,\ev _1)\). Thus identifications of functors are equivalently natural isomorphisms of functors.

Proof

Proof. This functor factors as \(C \xrightarrow {i} \Iso (C) \xrightarrow {\pi _{\Iso }} \Ar (C)\). The first functor is an equivalence by the Rezk axiom, while the second one is an embedding by Lemma 2.3.3. The claim follows. □

Agda Factor the identity-arrow functor

Derivation, checked

identityIso-arrow : {C : CAT} → (isoArrow ∘ identityIso) =₁ (identityArrow {C})
Proof / implementation
identityIso-arrow {C} = constant-restriction d₀ ∙
  ((edge₀ ◁ pullbackLift-β₁ (Identity.common-edge C)) ∙
  (comp-assoc (Identity.triangles C) pullback₁ edge₀ ∙
    (((edge₀ ∘ pullback₁) ◁ pullbackLift-β₁ (Identity.identities C)) ∙
      comp-assoc identityIso isoTriangles (edge₀ ∘ pullback₁))))
